findings.title: useState called after an early return
findings.explanation: When user is null the component returns before useState; when user later becomes non-null (typical after loading) the render calls one more hook than the previous render and React throws 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render', crashing the component. The rules-of-hooks lint rule is suppressed on the line, which is why tooling is silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Move useState(false) above the early return and keep the null check after all hooks. Remove the eslint-disable comment.

findings.title: Auto-save interval always saves the initial empty draft
findings.explanation: The effect runs once with deps [], so the interval callback closes over draft from the first render (""). Every 5 seconds save('') is called regardless of what the user typed, so the draft is never saved and may overwrite saved data with an empty string. The exhaustive-deps rule is suppressed with no justification. The same stale reference applies to the save prop.
findings.suggested_fix: Add draft and save to the dependency array (the interval is recreated on change), or keep the latest draft/save in refs updated each render and read them in the interval. Remove the eslint-disable comment.

findings.title: Resize listener is never removed
findings.explanation: The effect adds a window resize listener but returns no cleanup. After the component unmounts the listener stays registered, keeps calling setWidth on an unmounted component and retains it in memory; with remounts (or StrictMode double-invoke) listeners accumulate.
findings.suggested_fix: Return a cleanup: return () => window.removeEventListener("resize", onResize);

limitations: Only three source files, package.json and tsconfig.json exist; no ESLint config or Next.js config was present.
Static reading only; nothing was executed.
Callers of these components were not available, so how often user flips from null to non-null in Profile is assumed from the prop type.
